images.title: Two equal factors, one shape
images.purpose: Shows the simplest resize: a 3 by 2 rectangle with width and height both multiplied by 2 becomes a 6 by 4 rectangle of the same shape.
images.composition: One large rectangle with a smaller rectangle nested in its bottom left corner, a horizontal slider under them and a vertical slider to their right. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A teal (#0072B2) rectangle 3 units wide and 2 units high sits in the bottom left corner of a larger green (#009E73) outlined rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units high; the two share the bottom left corner. Side labels: '3' under the bottom edge of the small rectangle, '2' beside its left edge, '6' under the bottom edge of the large rectangle, '4' beside its right edge. A dark outline colour (#2B2B2B) horizontal slider track under the figure has one reddish purple (#CC79A7) round knob, with the label 'width factor 2'. A dark outline colour vertical slider track to the right has one reddish purple round knob, with the label 'height factor 2'. Above the figure the label 'ratio 3 : 2 kept'. Exactly 2 rectangles, 2 slider tracks, 2 knobs.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: When the width factor equals the height factor, the picture grows without stretching.
images.description: Shows the simplest resize: a 3 by 2 rectangle with width and height both multiplied by 2 becomes a 6 by 4 rectangle of the same shape.
images.teaching_notes: Keep the sliders plain; no numbers on the tracks other than the listed labels.

image_decisions.why: The practice tool's core move is choosing one factor for each side; one clear picture of equal factors keeping the shape anchors the practice.
